# A round-up interval from an interval of the default type

Kernel `upward_from_interval_1` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. No public operation calls it yet ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

The same set in the other storage: an interval of the default type, $X = [x_l, x_u]$, as a state of the round-up interval, $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$ stored as $(z_u, z_n)$; the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$, as the empty set, both lanes a NaN. Exact: the same members:

$$Z = X.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $Z$ as $(z_u, z_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [-z_n, z_u]$, stored as $(z_u, z_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval.
- $Z$ is the empty set, both lanes a NaN, exactly when $X$ is empty.
- $Z$ and $X$ have the same members; so for a nonempty $X$ the same bounds, $-z_n = x_l$ and $z_u = x_u$, exactly, as extended real numbers (a zero bound may change its sign).

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_from_interval_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_from_interval_1.kernel), the description the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) is generated from. The generator prints no C++ of it yet. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)). A line of two statements separated by ` | ` is a *pair line*: the two lanes of one instruction, lane 0 on the left ([the pair form](../developer/design/upward.md#the-pair-form)).

```
# A default interval Interval<T, 1> [xl, xu] as a state of the round-up interval
# (docs/developer/design/upward.md, "Conversions"): (xu, -xl), and the default empty set
# (+inf, -inf) as (NaN, NaN). Exact, in every rounding mode: the same set, the signs of zero bounds
# aside. Requires the rounding mode upward set by kairn::upward::Scope and the options of
# docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang -frounding-math, MSVC /fp:strict).

e  = eq(xl, const inf)                                         # its empty set
nl = neg(xl)
zu = select(e, const nan, xu) | zn = select(e, const nan, nl)  # (xu, -xl): a make
```
